Hell Let Loose is a World War II shooter that prioritizes realism, teamwork, and communication over fast-paced action. Matches are slow, tense, and often brutal. Success depends less on individual skill and more on coordination between squads, commanders, and support roles.

The scale of battles is impressive. Large maps, long sightlines, and deadly weapons create an atmosphere where every movement feels risky. Dying is quick and often sudden, reinforcing the importance of strategy and positioning. When teamwork clicks, the game delivers some of the most immersive multiplayer moments available.

The downside is accessibility. The game does very little to teach new players, and without communication, matches can feel chaotic and confusing. Performance and bugs can also disrupt immersion. Hell Let Loose is incredibly rewarding—but only if you’re willing to commit.

Ever wanted to machine gun and have it feel like it should? Suppression MATTERS! Not to mention one round kills in the chest in this game. A+ Game for the patient gamer willing to learn. Performance issues could partly be due to my outdated pc hardware, but I think it just magnifies the issues that are present. This is the most realistic WW2 FPS game I've played to date. Atmosphere, sound, gunplay, everything just adds to the intensity and feeling that you could die at any point and it's amazing. Class roles are well done and communicating with the different roles is crucial. Don't expect to play this like COD or Battlefield AT ALL. Don't expect to see everyone or get 10+ kills a game, and expect to run and get shot and not know where it came from.

The community is really friendly and I've had some good laughs through listening to others' voice comms.
Communicating to attack/defend is always a good time and while the games can be long (1 hour+), it really feels like you bonded with your squadmates by the end of the match, especially after a hard-earned or last-minute clutch win.

Overall, a great hardcore WW2 FPS game all around.

Also the whistling of the artillery and not knowing if its gonna kill you until it drops is terrifying.

Leave it in your wish list until they fix it. Once it's fixed, it'll be one of the best games you've ever played.

Its more hardcore than Battlefield or COD but more casual than Squad or Arma. Unfortunately the player base for the most part has zero interest in playing anything strategically. Theres a decent amount of people who use mics but there isnt enough communication. Tank roles are usually empty and sniper roles are usually just someone sniping instead of playing with a scout like the game intends. As for commander half the time nobody wants the role. It seems like HLL is a blend of casual and hardcore fps war sims but you still get the casual playerbase of cod and battlefield for the most part.

Update 14

British equipment has been actively butchered and is riddled with questionable design choices, without even getting into the bizarre and blatant disregard for equipment used by the UK in WWII.

This update plays and feels as though there was little to zero play testing, with the Pattern 14 Enfield (which shouldn't even be present in the game) functioning as a carbon copy of the Karabiner 98K, and the Rifle No.4 (an absolute staple of British firearms across WWII) being so wildly unreliable and weak that the Lanchester machine-gun (which also shouldn't even be here) is more functional at range. Having briefly used the Rifle No.4 and Jungle Carbine, I also can't help but notice that both guns feel utterly identical, leaving zero practical reason to use one over the other.

The British in this game need desperate reworking to the point I wouldn't recommend buying it in this condition, especially not if you were hoping to play as the British. Team 17 is setting a painfully low bar for the quality of content to come.

Hell Let Loose, a game that fills this gals need for a World War II sim. The game is fantastic in every way possible. The graphics are crisp and clean, the game-play is fun and intense, community is fun to interact with. Hell Let Loose has what you want and what you need. Tanks and infantry combat going hand-and-hand. All while being supported by a development team that shows true compassion and care for their baby. And with the coming update that is adding an amazing new map, as well new content; light tanks. This game is soooo much fun.

Hell Let Loose is a must have for any fan of WWII or fans of FPS/SIMS in general.
I rate HLL a high 9/10 with a massive 𝓛𝓲𝓵𝓵𝔂 seal of approval!

Go pick up your copy today, you will not be disappointed!

This update is a poorly tested unbalanced mess. British units cannot do anything to German units when German units get a hold on a ridge line over a point, the biggest offender being El-Alamein, giant open areas with minimal if ANY cover leads to German MG soldiers to just mow down British units. Beyond that German units get all around better weapons and equipment, semi-auto rifles, MG42s and better range with their bolt rifles. Meanwhile British units are stuck with all around worse equipment, mainly low fire rate smgs, low mag capacity mgs, and the Enfield rifle. British units equipped with the Lee-Enfield unit do not use the Mad Minute grip that was trained with it, reducing the firerate of the Enfield to that of your average bolt action rifle, making it unable to compete with the equipment German Units get.

I recommend avoiding playing British v. German maps until there are changes made due to the fact that even the bare minimum amount of cohesion is needed for a German team completely crush a British team.

After playing Squad for almost 300 hours, and wanting to get into a WW2 version of it... my life is now complete with Hell Let Loose!

HLL is a blend between hardcore milsim and a more arcade shooter because it focuses on strategy and tactics and very quick time-to-kill, but it also has a simplified movement system and controls in general.

The mechanics of the game are great and are being focused more-and-more on gameplay than on realism (where it doesn't make sense to make it more realistic at the cost of gameplay). A great example of this is how garrisons are destroyable by explosives, but outposts (rallypoints in Squads) are not... the enemy needs to walk into a certain radius of an outpost to destroy it. This allows for nice flanking and behind-enemy-lines attacks, without allowing the commander to simply bomb the outpost to remove it.

I could talk a lot more about this game, but basically, if you liked Squad / Post Scriptum / Verdun, etc, then you HAVE to try this game. You will love it.
Excellent game which balances perfectly what all previous WWII FPS games have done well. Excellent maps. Great community as well. Top notch!
